I was using a camera tripod to test out different lengths of a rifle and what I noticed is yes SBRs (11.5" / 10.3") give more mobility in tighter spaces however the gain is only fraction of a second of the effort needed to get a 14.5" or 16" around the same scenario. However in any scenario where you're not in a complicated tight space, all that goes out the window. So yes, in a mostly indoor space SBRs have an advantage.

However the advantage that I did not expect is SBRs are considerably easier to keep held up for longer periods of time, and a lot easier to keep held steady while focusing on a target etc. What I noticed was 11.5" / 10.3" was overkill however 14.5" over 16" is when I began to notice effort needed to keep the gun up and on target, even with a plastic tripod.

I went back and confirmed watching a hickok45 video shooting the DDM4A1 (14.5") vs the DDM4V7 (16") and I noticed the same thing. He more often kept the 14.5" held up, and higher, and more often dropped the 16" asap and held it lower.

So this made me think, the 14.5" / SBRs main advantage is not that they are short barrel, but that they are easier to hold up and keep on target. Which made me think, one of the most important things on a tactical rifle is to keep weight off of the front of it. So it's not only advantageous to have a 14.5" over 16" (even if pinned), but you should also try to keep the rail length minimal just for a hand guard and sufficient front iron sight.
